summary: This Docusaurus plugin automatically creates individual routes for each article series at build time, so that URLs like `/series/my-series-name` work properly. Instead of using a single dynamic route with a parameter, it generates one real route per series, which allows Docusaurus's link checker to verify that series links are valid without having to ignore broken links site-wide.

explanations.32: This loads Node's built-in path utility for working with file paths across different operating systems.
explanations.33: This imports a helper function that scans the blog articles and extracts all the unique series names (slugs) from their metadata.
explanations.35: A Docusaurus plugin is a function that receives configuration context and returns an object describing what the plugin does.
explanations.41: This method tells Docusaurus to watch for changes in blog article files, so new series are detected and routes are created even while the dev server is running.
explanations.44: This method runs after content is loaded during the build process, triggering the main logic to create routes.
explanations.45: This loops through every unique series slug that was found by scanning the article metadata.
explanations.46: For each series, this tells Docusaurus to create a new route that maps a URL path to a React component.
explanations.47: This is the actual URL pattern—for a series slug 'writing-tips', this would create the route `/series/writing-tips`.
explanations.48: This specifies which React component should be rendered when someone visits that series route; the component receives the slug and uses it to fetch and display relevant articles.
explanations.49: Setting `exact: true` means this route only matches the exact path—it won't match `/series/writing-tips/foo` or similar variations.
